title.en: Refraction at spherical surfaces and lenses

hook.en: An optician grinds glass to a chosen curvature and gives you exactly +2 dioptres. How does the shape of the glass decide its power?
hook.kn: ದೃಗ್ವಿಜ್ಞಾನಿ ಗಾಜನ್ನು ನಿರ್ದಿಷ್ಟ ವಕ್ರತೆಗೆ ಉಜ್ಜಿ ನಿಖರವಾಗಿ +2 ಡಯಾಪ್ಟರ್ ಕನ್ನಡಕ ಕೊಡುತ್ತಾರೆ. ಗಾಜಿನ ಆಕಾರ ಸಾಮರ್ಥ್ಯವನ್ನು ಹೇಗೆ ನಿರ್ಧರಿಸುತ್ತದೆ?

say.en: An optician grinds glass to a chosen curvature and gives you exactly plus 2 dioptres. How does the shape of the glass decide its power? In this lesson: Use refraction at a single spherical surface.
Derive and apply the lens maker's formula.
Use the thin lens formula, power and combinations.

body.en: For a *spherical surface* of radius $R$ separating media $n_1$ (object side) and $n_2$, the object and image distances satisfy $n_2/v - n_1/u = (n_2 - n_1)/R$. Applying it to both surfaces of a thin lens gives the lens maker's formula $1/f = (n_{21} - 1)(1/R_1 - 1/R_2)$.
body.kn: ಗೋಳೀಯ ಮೇಲ್ಮೈಯಲ್ಲಿ n₂/v − n₁/u = (n₂ − n₁)/R. ಎರಡೂ ಮೇಲ್ಮೈಗಳಿಗೆ ಅನ್ವಯಿಸಿದರೆ ಮಸೂರ ತಯಾರಕರ ಸೂತ್ರ ಸಿಗುತ್ತದೆ.

narration.en: For a spherical surface of radius R separating media n_1 (object side) and n_2, the object and image distances satisfy n_2/v - n_1/u = (n_2 - n_1)/R. Applying it to both surfaces of a thin lens gives the lens maker's formula 1/f = (n_{21} - 1)(1/R_1 - 1/R_2).
narration.kn: ಗೋಳೀಯ ಮೇಲ್ಮೈಯಲ್ಲಿ n₂/v − n₁/u = (n₂ − n₁)/R. ಎರಡೂ ಮೇಲ್ಮೈಗಳಿಗೆ ಅನ್ವಯಿಸಿದರೆ ಮಸೂರ ತಯಾರಕರ ಸೂತ್ರ ಸಿಗುತ್ತದೆ.

say.en: For a spherical surface of radius R separating media n 1 object side and n 2, the object and image distances satisfy n 2 over v - n 1 over u equals (n 2 - n 1)/R. Applying it to both surfaces of a thin lens gives the lens maker's formula 1 over f equals n 21 minus 1(1 over R 1 minus 1 over R 2). n 2 over v - n 1 over u equals (n 2 - n 1)/R.
say.kn: ಗೋಳೀಯ ಮೇಲ್ಮೈಯಲ್ಲಿ n 2 over v - n 1 over u equals (n 2 - n 1)/R. ಎರಡೂ ಮೇಲ್ಮೈಗಳಿಗೆ ಅನ್ವಯಿಸಿದರೆ ಮಸೂರ ತಯಾರಕರ ಸೂತ್ರ ಸಿಗುತ್ತದೆ.

narration.en: Drag the tip of the object. One ray runs parallel to the axis and bends through the focus; another goes straight through the centre. Where they meet is the image.
narration.kn: ವಸ್ತುವಿನ ತುದಿಯನ್ನು ಎಳೆಯಿರಿ. ಒಂದು ಕಿರಣ ಅಕ್ಷಕ್ಕೆ ಸಮಾಂತರವಾಗಿ ಬಂದು ನಾಭಿಯ ಮೂಲಕ ಬಾಗುತ್ತದೆ; ಇನ್ನೊಂದು ಕೇಂದ್ರದ ಮೂಲಕ ನೇರವಾಗಿ ಹೋಗುತ್ತದೆ. ಅವು ಸೇರುವಲ್ಲಿ ಬಿಂಬ.

caption.en: Drag the yellow ring at the tip of the object. The ray parallel to the axis bends through F; the ray through the centre goes straight on. They meet at the image, where 1/v − 1/u = 1/f. Inside F the rays spread out: trace them back (dashed) to a virtual image.
caption.kn: ವಸ್ತುವಿನ ತುದಿಯ ಹಳದಿ ಉಂಗುರವನ್ನು ಎಳೆಯಿರಿ. ಅಕ್ಷಕ್ಕೆ ಸಮಾಂತರ ಕಿರಣ F ಮೂಲಕ ಬಾಗುತ್ತದೆ; ಕೇಂದ್ರದ ಮೂಲಕದ ಕಿರಣ ನೇರವಾಗಿ ಹೋಗುತ್ತದೆ. ಅವು ಬಿಂಬದಲ್ಲಿ ಸೇರುತ್ತವೆ. F ಒಳಗೆ ಕಿರಣಗಳು ಹರಡುತ್ತವೆ: ಹಿಂದಕ್ಕೆ (ಚುಕ್ಕೆ ಗೆರೆ) ಮಿಥ್ಯ ಬಿಂಬಕ್ಕೆ.

text.en: Object at F: the rays come out parallel, image at infinity
text.kn: ವಸ್ತು F ನಲ್ಲಿ: ಕಿರಣಗಳು ಸಮಾಂತರ, ಬಿಂಬ ಅನಂತದಲ್ಲಿ

narration.en: Let us draw a ray diagram for a convex lens and confirm it with the lens formula.

say.en: Draw the axis and a convex lens. Mark the foci F and the points 2F on both sides.
Put the object beyond 2F. A ray parallel to the axis passes through the far focus after refraction.
A ray through the optical centre goes straight on. The rays meet between F and 2F: a real, inverted, smaller image.
Lens formula with signs: u = −30 cm and f = +12 cm.
So v = 20 cm and m = −0.67, exactly what the diagram shows.
The lens maker's formula gives f from the surfaces. With both radii 20 cm and n = 1.5, f = 20 cm and power P = 5 dioptre.

title.en: Thin lens formula, power and combinations

body.en: For a *thin lens* $1/v - 1/u = 1/f$ and $m = v/u$. Power $P = 1/f$, in dioptres when $f$ is in metres; convex lenses have positive power. Thin lenses in contact add their powers: $P = P_1 + P_2 + \dots$, and the total magnification is the product of the individual magnifications.
body.kn: ತೆಳು ಮಸೂರ ಸೂತ್ರ 1/v − 1/u = 1/f, m = v/u. ಸಾಮರ್ಥ್ಯ P = 1/f (ಡಯಾಪ್ಟರ್). ಸಂಪರ್ಕದಲ್ಲಿರುವ ಮಸೂರಗಳ ಸಾಮರ್ಥ್ಯಗಳು ಕೂಡುತ್ತವೆ.

points.en: P = P₁ + P₂ for *lenses* in contact

narration.en: For a thin lens 1/v - 1/u = 1/f and m = v/u. Power P = 1/f, in dioptres when f is in metres; convex lenses have positive power. Thin lenses in contact add their powers: P = P_1 + P_2 + \dots, and the total magnification is the product of the individual magnifications.
narration.kn: ತೆಳು ಮಸೂರ ಸೂತ್ರ 1/v − 1/u = 1/f, m = v/u. ಸಾಮರ್ಥ್ಯ P = 1/f (ಡಯಾಪ್ಟರ್). ಸಂಪರ್ಕದಲ್ಲಿರುವ ಮಸೂರಗಳ ಸಾಮರ್ಥ್ಯಗಳು ಕೂಡುತ್ತವೆ.

say.en: For a thin lens 1 over v minus 1 over u equals 1 over f and m equals v over u. Power P equals 1 over f, in dioptres when f is in metres; convex lenses have positive power. Thin lenses in contact add their powers: P equals P 1 plus P 2 plus \dots, and the total magnification is the product of the individual magnifications.
say.kn: ತೆಳು ಮಸೂರ ಸೂತ್ರ 1 over v minus 1 over u equals 1 over f, m equals v over u. ಸಾಮರ್ಥ್ಯ P equals 1 over f (ಡಯಾಪ್ಟರ್). ಸಂಪರ್ಕದಲ್ಲಿರುವ ಮಸೂರಗಳ ಸಾಮರ್ಥ್ಯಗಳು ಕೂಡುತ್ತವೆ.

say.en: P equals 1 over f m in D.
P equals P 1 plus P 2 for lenses in contact.

aim.en: To find the focal length of a convex lens by plotting graphs between u and v and between 1/u and 1/v. Try this: Find the point where u = v on the u–v graph: it lies at 2f, so halve it to get f.

heading.en: Refraction at Spherical Surfaces and Lenses

tagline.en: Refraction at a single spherical surface, the lens maker's formula, the thin lens formula, magnification, power and combinations of thin lenses in contact.

myth.en: The lens formula is 1/v + 1/u = 1/f, the same as for a mirror, and magnification is −v/u.

truth.en: For a thin lens, 1/v − 1/u = 1/f and m = v/u. For a mirror, 1/v + 1/u = 1/f and m = −v/u. In a mirror the light turns back, so the real image is on the same side as the object; in a lens it goes on through, so the real image is on the far side (v > 0). The signs in the formulas take care of this.

say.en: Single surface: $\frac{n_2}{v} - \frac{n_1}{u} = \frac{n_2 - n_1}{R}$.
Lens maker: $\frac{1}{f} = (n_{21} - 1)\left(\frac{1}{R_1} - \frac{1}{R_2}\right)$; the focal length depends on the surrounding medium.
Thin lens: $\frac{1}{v} - \frac{1}{u} = \frac{1}{f}$; $m = \frac{v}{u}$.
Power P = 1/f (f in metres), unit dioptre; lenses in contact: P = P1 + P2, m = m1 m2.

narration.en: Many people think: The lens formula is 1/v + 1/u = 1/f, the same as for a mirror, and magnification is −v/u. Actually: For a thin lens, 1/v − 1/u = 1/f and m = v/u. For a mirror, 1/v + 1/u = 1/f and m = −v/u. In a mirror the light turns back, so the real image is on the same side as the object; in a lens it goes on through, so the real image is on the far side (v > 0). The signs in the formulas take care of this.

problem.en: An object is 30 cm in front of a convex lens of focal length 10 cm. Find the image position and magnification.

answer.en: 15 cm on the other side; real, inverted, half size

narration.en: Let us solve this together. An object is 30 cm in front of a convex lens of focal length 10 cm. Find the image position and magnification.

say.en: Let us solve this together. An object is 30 centimetres in front of a convex lens of focal length 10 centimetres. Find the image position and magnification.
u equals minus 30 centimetres, f = plus 10 centimetres.
1 over v equals 1 over f plus 1 over u equals 1 over 10 minus 1 over 30 equals 1 over 15, so v = plus 15 centimetres.
m equals v over u equals 15 over minus 30 equals minus 0.5.
So the answer is 15 centimetres on the other side; real, inverted, half size.

problem.en: A biconvex lens (n = 1.5) has R₁ = 10 cm and R₂ = −15 cm. Find its focal length and power.

narration.en: Let us solve this together. A biconvex lens (n = 1.5) has R₁ = 10 cm and R₂ = −15 cm. Find its focal length and power.

say.en: Let us solve this together. A biconvex lens n equals 1.5 has R 1 equals 10 centimetres and R 2 equals minus 15 centimetres. Find its focal length and power.
1 over f equals 1.5 minus 1(1 over 10 minus 1 over minus 15) equals 0.5 times (1 over 10 plus 1 over 15).
1 over f equals 0.5 times 5 over 30 equals 1 over 12, so f equals 12 centimetres.
P equals 1 over 0.12 is approximately plus 8.3 D.
So the answer is f equals 12 centimetres, P is approximately plus 8.3 D.
